profiles.name: Louis G. Mische
profiles.query: "Louis G. Mische" IWW 1919 portrait photograph
profiles.identity_context: Louis G. Mische was an Industrial Workers of the World organizer detained during the First Red Scare. The One Big Union Monthly names him among IWW detainees transferred from Seattle to Ellis Island in February 1919 for deportation proceedings. His son, Catonsville Nine activist George Mische, later recalled that his father had also been jailed in Spokane and had used the name Karl Schmidt. In that oral history, George described the threatened deportation as ultimately defeated when his father’s birth in Cleveland was established. The exact detention and release dates have not been confirmed.
profiles.finding: FamilySearch EugeneMische1931–1997 names fatherLouisGage40 andCeceliaKahl; familyrecord alone insufficient to link portrait to IWWdetainee; no image verified.
